rows.sourceContext: D13 record number 01, geometry /territories/0: SW04 and S05 joins, legitimate NW/N bay, eastern mountain terrain. Reference visually shows continuous southern mainland.

findings.observation: Former broad SW/S water and lower harbour have been replaced by continuous mainland; no water band interrupts the lower developed landscape.

findings.check: Preserve legitimate water and eastern terrain
findings.observation: Large NW/N bay remains, with the main waterside harbour and eastern mountain wall retained.
Both mine pits and the tank/flare/solar landmark groups remain identifiable in their broad original arrangement. Mineral identity and productive capacity cannot be verified from appearance.
Added foreground reads as connected hills, woods, grassland and paths. No conspicuous new industrial complex or stranded/floating harbour was seen.
1254-square composition and recognizable fine scene details remain; some detail and texture were repainted, so this is not an unchanged-pixel claim.

uncertainties: Exact shoreline position, national border and camera correspondence remain unregistered.
New local hills and paths are illustrative and not verified against a heightfield or road network.
Facility existence, ownership, resource type, reserves, production and runtime status are not established by the image.

rows.sourceContext: D13 record number 09, geometry /territories/8: genuine W/NW coast and southern land joins to 19/20; no broad southern sea boundary.

findings.observation: Continuous land reaches the full lower foreground; broad southern coastal wrapping is removed.
Substantial western sea and the indented western shoreline remain. Repair did not erase the whole coast.

Three readily identifiable pit complexes, the lower-central industrial group, central domed settlement and river/bridge sequence remain in their broad original arrangement. Appearance does not establish the four brief resource identities.
Added southern land blends as woodland, rock, grass and paths. Existing western harbour remains connected to sea; removed southern harbour leaves no obvious floating or landlocked pier remnant.
1254-square scene retains readable principal structures, fields, coast and terrain. Texture is somewhat repainted; exact sharpness equivalence is not claimed.

uncertainties: Exact southern boundary and W-coast scale cannot be measured from the oblique illustration.
New foreground terrain/path detail is illustrative, not verified topographic or infrastructure data.
Facility existence, ownership, resource type, reserves, production and runtime status are not established by the image.

rows.sourceContext: D13 geometry /territories/37: real western island bodies; mainland S44 and SE45 joins, N/E mainland. Reference frame crosses map x=0; black padding is not sea.

findings.observation: The former southern separating water band is replaced by continuous wooded/rocky mainland.
Both principal western island groups remain visibly water-separated; the broad western sea was not filled.

Upper-right mine, central campus/town, upper-middle solar panels, gas-sphere complex, lower-right turbines and western oil/industrial island remain recognizable; island and mainland ports still meet water.
Added southern hills, fields, paths and small buildings read as contiguous terrain. No stranded pier or conspicuous new industrial complex was observed.
Mine terraces/equipment, campus roofs, turbines, panels and shoreline detail remain readable. Textures and minor decorative detail changed, but no conspicuous scene-wide softening prevents approval.

uncertainties: Exact southern boundary and camera correspondence remain unregistered.
Added local foreground terrain/buildings are illustrative, not verified infrastructure.
Black reference padding is excluded from geography interpretation.

rows.sourceContext: D13 geometry /territories/39: local S water opening; SW45 and SE46 mainland joins; N/E mainland. Eleven grid coast edges do not specify photographic bay size.

findings.observation: Substantial connected land now frames both sides of the southern harbour and continues off the image sides/bottom.
A single bounded harbour pocket and narrow southern exit remain. The valid opening was not removed, and broad SW/S sea wrapping is no longer present.
Upper-left mine, lower-left tank/oil complex, right-middle rail hub, river/bridges, towns and the southern harbour are identifiable in their broad original arrangement.
Harbour boats and piers remain in water with an exit; no obvious stranded pier or new implausible industrial complex was seen.
Rail-yard tracks/roofs, mine terraces, tank edges, field rows and harbour cranes remain legible. Some terrain detail is repainted/stylized, without conspicuous overall blur.

uncertainties: Harbour pocket size and channel width are not camera-calibrated; approval is for a local opening with mainland flanks, not a measured match to 11 grid edges.
Harbour navigability, ship dimensions and actual port operation are not established.
The local southern water pocket does not assert ownership of neighboring land.

rows.sourceContext: D13 geometry /territories/41: NW/W/SW narrow watercourse with nearby opposing land, genuine SE sea, E43 mainland/mountain relation and a local S47 land join.

findings.observation: A clear near opposite bank replaces the unbounded western sea; the water corridor is not erased.
The candidate has a visibly connected lower foreground land tongue rather than water isolating the full southern flank. The exact source S47 join cannot be positioned pixel-for-pixel.
The lower-right harbour and broad southeast water remain, while eastern mountain/mainland terrain is retained.

Upper-left solar/turbine group, upper-right pit, middle-left mine/industrial group, lower-right turbines, lower gas-sphere complex, railway and southeast port remain identifiable. The small former upper-left dock is removed, with no stranded remnant; it is not one of the principal source-brief facilities.
Added western bank and southern terrain read as continuous forested/rocky land. Southeast port structures still meet water; no obvious floating or dry-land harbour was seen.

Mine conveyors/terraces, solar-panel divisions, turbine blades, rail scene and harbour detail remain distinguishable. Fine decorative detail is repainted, but no conspicuous overall loss of clarity was observed.

uncertainties: River width, camera orientation and exact S47 join placement remain unregistered.
The river route/near bank is approved as coarse morphology, not surveyed river geometry or navigability.
Added opposing-bank terrain does not establish country ownership or economic infrastructure.
